newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BUTINGES SAYS CONSTRUCTION ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: BUTINGES SAYS CONSTRUCTION ON TRACK.

text.p: Lithuania's Butinges Nafta said on Monday that the construction of an oil terminal on the country's Baltic coast was on track and would be completed by October 1998.
"The work is going on as scheduled and in October 1998 it will be over," Vladislovas Gedvilas, the company's director general, told a news conference.
He said that construction on the sea-part of the terminal will begin early next summer.
He also said that the company's financial situation was looking up and that there was enough investor interest to complete the construction.
But he added that lenders wanted state-guarantees.
He also said that the government had subscribed to 34.1 percent of the company's fourth share issue, which will raise its share capital to around 260 million litas from 72 million litas.
Gedvilas said he was confident that the rest of the issue would be distributed successfully, noting that a number of international and domestic companies had expressed interest in it.
The Lithuanian companies include chemical producer Achema and the Lithuanian Savings Bank. The international firms include Flour Daniels.
The Lithuanian government earlier said that it would reduce its stake in the terminal to a minority holding.
The project has struggled to find investors and some analysts doubt that it will be able to compete with other Baltic terminals for the transit trade in Russian oil.
